title: S&P Global Stock: Buy, Hold, or Sell? | SPGI Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether S&P Global is finally a buying opportunity in October and answers no, reiterating the AVOID stance he last gave on 19 Aug 2026. The stock is down more than 18% in 2026 and has not recovered from the SaaS-apocalypse lows, even though some peers have. The business itself is formidable: sales have tripled from $5 billion in 2017 to more than $16 billion trailing, operating margins recently ran at about 44% with a plan to add roughly 50 basis points, and management is at peak headcount while using AI to raise output per employee. Usage is shifting from seat-based pricing to consumption and API usage rose fivefold between Q1 and Q2, but monetisation of that shift is unproven, and ratings growth is guided only to low-to-mid single digits as higher rates delay bond issuance. The decisive problem is returns and price: return on invested capital has fallen from above 35% before 2022 to about 10.5%, barely above the cost of capital, and his updated discounted cash flow fair value is $311 against a $403 market price, even though a 19.95x forward P/E looks superficially fair. Call made: SPGI AVOID at $403 (DCF $311), first tracked Parkevtate SPGI call, no flip. Based on the captions analysis recorded in the 19:00 run on 2026-10-13.

calls.base_case: DCF fair value $311 vs $403 market; forward P/E 19.95 looks fairly priced but rich on DCF. Sales tripled $5B (2017) to $16B+ TTM; operating margin ~44%, guided +~50bp.
calls.bull_case: Strong data-quality moat; API usage up 5x Q1->Q2 as business shifts seat-based to consumption pricing; ratings guided low-to-mid single-digit growth.
calls.bear_case: ROIC fell from 35%+ pre-2022 to ~10.5%, barely above WACC; higher rates delay bond issuance; consumption-model monetisation still unproven.
